archetype.name: Lost Season (with a Rookie of the Year)
archetype.definition: A 26-56 year in which Dallas never had a winning month, collapsed after January, and came away mainly with Cooper Flagg's Rookie of the Year campaign.

report.headline: Flagg won Rookie of the Year; the offense around him came apart

recap.finish: 26-56; missed the postseason, tied with New Orleans for third in the Southwest
recap.body:
This was a bad team, not an unlucky one. Dallas finished 26-56 with a Net Rtg of -5.3 (23rd), and its point margin implied 28 wins, so close games cost it about two. The site ranked it 24th of 30. The problem was the offense. A 111.2 offensive rating ranked 27th, against a 20th-ranked defense that was only slightly worse than the league average.

The season came in two parts. Dallas started 6-15 after a 4-12 November. It then played near break-even ball for two months, going 6-7 in December and 7-8 in January, and reached 19-30 still looking competitive. Then the floor gave way. February went 2-8 and March 3-14, which included the season's 10-game losing streak. In those months the defense bled 124.7 and then 122.88 points a game. The team never won more than four in a row all year.

The shot profile explains the offense. Dallas took 35.5% of its shots from three, 26th in the league and six points under the league average. It made only 34.4% of them, also 26th. That produced a 52.7 eFG % (27th). The team did get to the line, with a FT Rate that ranked 6th, but free throws couldn't make up for a poor shooting diet. It also gave itself few second chances: ORB % ranked 26th. The defense did one thing well, holding opponents to 35% from three (5th). It forced almost nothing, though: Opp TOV % ranked 27th, and opposing centers scored about two points over their usual averages against it.

Cooper Flagg carried the year: 1,473 points, 316 assists and the Rookie of the Year award, ranking 15th of 96 on the small forwards tab. He did it on a heavy load (26.9 USG %) at modest efficiency (54.8 TS %). The most productive group was the frontcourt, graded C-, with 13.5 combined Win Shares. Daniel Gafford (67.7 TS %) and Marvin Bagley III (66.1 TS %, 3.8 Win Shares) finished efficiently. Anthony Davis, 8th on his tab, appeared in only 20 games. The backcourt graded D and the wings D+. Ryan Nembhard ran the offense at 49.2 TS %, and Klay Thompson hit 202 threes but produced 0.5 Win Shares in 1,497 minutes.

The finish was loose rather than better. Over the last five games Dallas scored 122.6 a game and allowed 124.6, and it closed with a 149-128 win over Chicago. Through the decline the trend line was steady: 50-32 two years ago, 39-43 last year, 26-56 now. The offensive rating fell from 114.8 to 111.2 in a single season.

highlights.title: Flagg's Rookie of the Year season
highlights.body: Flagg led the team in minutes and points and ranked 15th of 96 at his position as a rookie, the clearest asset the year produced. His efficiency trailed his volume, which is typical for a first-year player carrying a weak offense. The talent is the part that should carry forward.

highlights.title: Efficient bigs held the frontcourt up
highlights.body: The frontcourt was the only group to grade above D-level and produced the most Win Shares of the three. Gafford and Bagley finished plays at elite rates, and Bagley ranked 21st of 93 on his tab. They score near the rim and don't create their own shots, so this group's value depends on someone else creating for them.

highlights.title: Perimeter defense contested threes
highlights.body: Opponents shot 35% from three, 5th-best in the league. This was the one area where the defense was clearly above average. It didn't add up to much, because the defense forced few turnovers and gave up a lot inside.

lowlights.title: A bottom-four offense built on twos
lowlights.body: A 27th-ranked offensive rating came from too few threes taken and too few made, plus little offensive rebounding. This was a structural shot-diet problem, not a slump: last year's offense ranked 17th, and the shooting fell away from it.

lowlights.title: February-March collapse
lowlights.body: After reaching 19-30 still within shouting distance, Dallas went 2-8 and then 3-14. That stretch included a 10-game losing streak, and the defense allowed more than 120 a game in both months. Whatever held the team together through December and January did not survive the second half.

lowlights.title: Guards and wings graded poorly
lowlights.body: The backcourt graded D and the wings D+. The minutes went to low-efficiency or low-impact players: Nembhard's 49.2 TS % at the point, and Thompson's 0.5 Win Shares despite heavy volume from three. Apart from Flagg and Naji Marshall, the perimeter gave Dallas little.

arc.note: A 6-15 start gave way to two near-.500 months that left Dallas 19-30 at the end of January. Then came a 2-8 February and a 3-14 March that sank the season.

recap.nextYear: The 26-56 record was close to honest: the margin implied 28 wins, so there is no hidden bounce-back to bank on. What carries forward is Flagg, the team's best and most-used player as a rookie, and an efficient pair of finishers in Gafford and Bagley. The work is on the perimeter, where both guard and wing groups graded D-level, and in the shot profile, which took and made too few threes for a modern offense. Davis ranked 8th at his position but played only 20 games, so his value is a question rather than a given. The defense was roughly average and did contest threes; it needs to force turnovers and protect the paint better. Three straight years of falling records and a sharp drop in offensive rating say the team needs real change rather than better luck."

confidence.note: Full 82-game season; margin and record agree.
